briefs.source_chain: US strikes Iranian air defense/comms near Hormuz while oil already rising in market hours, Iran hits military not energy targets, so crude/distillates/gas break out; that makes commodity inflation a front-end (not just term-premium) story, so a supply shock hits growth just as the Fed is pushed toward tightening, pressuring multiples; Europe is most exposed via gas plus spreading sub-NATO-threshold attacks; hardware (Dell/Broadcom) is the offsetting strength; outcome hinges on whether crude/gas/product prices fall (stabilization, conditional on NFP/CPI) or keep rising (sustained pressure).
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: Iran strikes near Hormuz during already-rising oil, Iran retaliates against military not energy, crude/distillates/gas rise; front-end pricing shift plus growth-vs-tightening squeeze pressures multiples; Europe most exposed via gas and spreading Russia-linked attacks; hardware (Dell, Palo Alto, Broadcom) is the offset; conclusion conditional on energy falling vs. rising, with NFP/CPI as the qualifier.

distortions.what: Brief folds Palo Alto Networks' guidance raise into the 'hardware' offset cluster; source lists it under a separate AI/Cyber Security section discussing Chain-of-Thought monitoring risk, which the brief omits entirely.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the fact (PANW raised guidance) is preserved correctly; only its topical grouping and the unrelated alignment/monitorability tangent are dropped.

distortions.what: Brief renders the conclusion as 'risk can recover' vs. source's more hedged 'risk has a path to recover'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same conditional invalidation (oil/gas/products falling, NFP/CPI cooperating) is preserved verbatim in substance.

briefs.source_chain: Risk-off tape (S&P -71bps, Brent to $95, yields up, 66% Sep hike odds) driven by Iran headlines; rising TTF gas supports a short gas-consumers-basket / long power-price-sensitive-utilities pair trade; Dell beats and raises F2027 AI-server and total revenue guidance, GS lifts F2027-29 EPS 38% and keeps Buy $425 PT; GS stays constructive on Europe (14.5x, 5.3% FCF yield) with sector OW/UW calls and upgrades DB to Buy (€43.75 PT) on a ~300bps 3yr ROTE improvement; sidebar on BTC ETF flows and the CLARITY Act vote.
briefs.brief_chain: Same top-line risk-off drivers and levels; same short-gas-consumers/long-utilities basket trade; same Dell beat-and-raise, 38% EPS lift, Buy $425 PT; same constructive Europe stance and DB upgrade to Buy on the ROTE thesis; same BTC/CLARITY Act sidebar.

distortions.what: Brief drops GS's explicit sector Overweight list (Technology, Banks, Defence, Telecoms, Renewables), Underweight list (Autos, Chemicals, Travel & Leisure, Healthcare), and the HALO pair trade.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — these are separate, secondary calls not tied to the note's lead themes (gas basket, Dell, DB); omitting them doesn't alter any call the brief does make.

distortions.what: Brief omits the DB price target (€43.75) while keeping the Buy upgrade and ROTE rationale.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — direction and rationale of the call are intact; only the specific target level is missing.

distortions.what: Brief omits the Anthropic cloud-computing deal item (Lambda/Nscale/Fluidstack/SpaceX) entirely.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — unconnected side item, not part of any call in the note.

distortions.what: Brief omits the memory/HBM chip-pricing debate, quote of the day, and stat of the day.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — supporting color, not a call or figure the brief's chain depends on.

briefs.source_chain: Renewed US-Iran strikes near Hormuz push Brent +4.60% to $94.65 and EU gas to a 3yr high of €72.22/MWh; that lifts DM yields to multi-year highs (bund, OAT, gilt, Treasury, JGB) and hits equities globally; Fed pricing turns more hawkish (64bps by June 2027, 69% Sept-hike odds vs. 27% on Aug 17), reinforced by Governor Barr; softer US data (ISM 54.6, JOLTS, quits) only briefly pauses the selloff; in Europe, sticky core CPI (2.4%) keeps ECB's Simkus hawkish; RBNZ hikes 25bps and strong Australian GDP firms up RBA hike bets.
briefs.brief_chain: Same causal chain end to end: Iran strikes drive oil/gas higher, which drives multi-year DM yield highs and a global equity selloff, hawkish Fed pricing reinforced by Barr, softer US data only a temporary pause, sticky Euro Area core CPI keeping the ECB hawkish via Simkus, RBNZ hike and strong Australian GDP firming RBA bets.

distortions.what: Brief drops the personal/holiday narrative opener, Bessent's Hormuz-bypass and Iran-sanctions remarks, UK gilt/fiscal-buffer and budget-date detail, JGB specifics, final PMI revisions, and the day-ahead data/earnings calendar.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — none of these change the stance, the Fed/ECB pricing calls, or the invalidation; they're secondary color and calendar housekeeping.

distortions.what: Brief states Fed pricing as a flat '64bps of hikes by June 2027' where source frames it as a same-day move ('up +5.1bps on the day to 64bps').
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — end-state figure (64bps, 69% Sept odds) is preserved correctly; only the day-over-day delta framing is compressed away.

briefs.source_chain: CTA/vol-control positioning is already high and vol-control equity allocations sit at the 100th percentile, so there is little room for further buying; BofA models systematic strategies selling in all three scenarios — $163bn sold in a down market, $1bn sold if flat, and $9bn sold even in an up market; GS's own one-month conditional projections agree (modest buying if up, violent unwind if down) and GS's current systematic length ($146.5bn) sits at the upper end of its 1yr range; McElligott calls the vol collapse 'epic' and flags possible trading-loss risk; buyback support is near its peak just as the September blackout window expands, removing a major incremental buyer — net message: selling risk dominates and there's little genuine buying support left, even on the upside.
briefs.brief_chain: Same setup (positioning high, vol-control maxed at 100th percentile) but states BofA shows systematics buying $9bn in an up market, then GS's conditional projections (modest buying if up, violent unwind if down) and current length at the upper end of the 1yr range, McElligott's 'epic' vol-collapse warning, and buyback fading into the September blackout.

distortions.what: Brief reports BofA's up-market figure as '$9bn bought in an up market'; the source states BofA modeled systematics selling $9bn even in an up market ('sell $163bn in a down market, sell $1bn if markets are flat, and sell $9bn in an up market') — the brief inverts sell to buy for that scenario.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — the note's whole thesis ('Sell sell or sell') is that systematic flow is a net seller across down, flat, and up scenarios, i.e. no scenario provides real buying support; the brief's inversion turns the up-market case into a (weak) buy signal, which softens the flow-headwind read a reader would act on.

distortions.what: Brief renders McElligott's warning as 'possible trading losses' vs. source's 'major trading losses may soon surface'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both convey a genuine risk warning; severity wording shift doesn't change what a reader would do with it.
